text.p: Nokia, Europe's largest mobile phone maker, said Monday a record second quarter helped its first-half profits surge to 3.33 billion markka ($599.7 million) and said it anticipated good full-year profitability.
Analysts polled by Reuters had expected Nokia's profits over the period to rise strongly from a weak 1.13 billion ($204 million) a year ago, to about three billion markka ($540 million).
The company said net sales bounded to 24.39 billion markka ($4.39 billion) from the weak 16.88 billion ($3.04 billion) year-ago level.
It said mobile phone sales rose 49 percent and its sales of telecommunicatons infrastructure "clearly surpassed market growth" by rising 35 percent.

"The results meet our performance targets and give us reason to maintain our previously stated positive outlook for strong growth and good profitability for the whole year," it said in a statement accompanying the results.

Nokia's profit report came as expectations had grown sharply after a surprise 44 percent surge in first-half profit last month from its Swedish rival, Ericsson, which had very fast growth in mobile handsets and benefited from currency gains.
